title.zh: 卷四十九 志第十八: 禮志一
title.raw: 卷四十九 志第十八: 禮志一 Volume 49 Treatises 19: Rites 1

sentences.zh: 禮志一

translations.literal: Rites Treatise, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Rites I

sentences.zh: 理自天設，情由人生。

translations.literal: Principle is established by Heaven; feeling arises from human life.
translations.idiomatic: Principle is ordained by Heaven, while human feeling springs from life among men.

sentences.zh: 以理制情，而禮樂之用行焉。

translations.literal: Using principle to restrain feeling, the function of rites and music is thereby put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: When principle governs feeling, the rites and music can fulfill their purpose.

sentences.zh: 林豺梁獺，是生郊禘；

translations.literal: Forests, jackals, beams, and otters — from these arose suburban and di sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Offerings in forests, jackals on beams, and otters in sacrifice gave rise to suburban and di rites;

sentences.zh: 窪尊燔黍，是生燕饗；

translations.literal: hollow vessels, roasting millet — from these arose banquets and feasts;
translations.idiomatic: earthen bowls and roasted millet gave rise to convivial feasts;

sentences.zh: 虆梩瓦棺，是生喪葬；

translations.literal: vine coffins and tile biers — from these arose mourning and burial;
translations.idiomatic: vine-woven biers and tile coffins gave rise to funeral rites;

sentences.zh: 儷皮緇布，是生婚冠。

translations.literal: paired skins and black cloth — from these arose marriage and capping.
translations.idiomatic: paired pelts and dark hemp gave rise to marriage and coming-of-age ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 皇造帝秩，三王彌文。

translations.literal: The August One fashioned the imperial order; the Three Kings ever more adorned it.
translations.idiomatic: The sage founders shaped the imperial order, and the Three Kings ever refined its ritual splendor.

sentences.zh: 一文一質，蓋本於忠。

translations.literal: One refinement, one plainness — all rooted in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Alternating ornament and simplicity, all grounded in sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 變通革弊，與時宜之，唯聖人為能通其意。

translations.literal: Transforming and adapting, reforming abuses, suiting the times — only the sage can penetrate its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: To adapt usage, reform abuses, and suit the age requires a sage who alone can grasp the full intent.

sentences.zh: 執理者膠瑟聚訟，不適人情；

translations.literal: Those who cling to principle bind the zither and gather lawsuits, ill-suited to human feeling;
translations.idiomatic: Those who cling rigidly to principle tie themselves in knots over ritual minutiae and fail to meet human needs;

sentences.zh: 徇情者梯稗綿蕝，不中天理。

translations.literal: those who indulge feeling use ladder-mats of barnyard grass and cotton rush mats, not hitting the mark of heavenly principle.
translations.idiomatic: while those who indulge mere sentiment offer crude mats of weeds and rushes and miss the mark of cosmic order.

sentences.zh: 秦漢而降，君子無取焉。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han downward, gentlemen took nothing from them.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qin and Han dynasties onward, men of discernment found nothing worth adopting in either extreme.

sentences.zh: 遼本朝鮮故壤，箕子八條之教，流風遺俗，蓋有存者。

translations.literal: Liao was originally the old territory of Korea; Jizi's Eight Articles of instruction — their lingering customs and surviving practices — surely had some who preserved them.
translations.idiomatic: Liao lay on what had once been Korean soil, and traces of Jizi's Eight Precepts and their customs still survived in places.

sentences.zh: 自其上世，緣情制宜，隱然有尚質之風。

translations.literal: From their upper generations, adapting measures to feeling, there was implicitly a wind of esteeming plainness.
translations.idiomatic: From earliest times they shaped institutions to human need and quietly upheld a spirit that favored simplicity.

sentences.zh: 遙輦胡剌可汗制祭山儀，蘇可汗制瑟瑟儀，阻午可汗制柴冊、再生儀。

translations.literal: The Yaolian Khala Khan established the Mountain Sacrifice Rite; Khan Su established the Sese Rite; Khan Zuowu established the Wood-Bundle and Rebirth rites.
translations.idiomatic: Khala Khan of the Yaolian line instituted the Mountain Sacrifice Rite, Khan Su the Sese Rite, and Khan Zuowu the Wood-Bundle and Rebirth rites.

sentences.zh: 其情樸，其用儉。

translations.literal: Their feeling was plain; their practice frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Their spirit was plain and their observance spare.

sentences.zh: 敬天恤災，施惠本孝，出於悃忱，殆有得於膠瑟聚訟之表者。

translations.literal: Revering Heaven, pitying disaster, bestowing grace rooted in filial piety, arising from sincere devotion — they perhaps attained what lies beyond binding the zither and gathering lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Revering Heaven, relieving disaster, and dispensing grace in the name of filial piety, they acted from sincere devotion and perhaps grasped what lies beyond empty ritual wrangling.

sentences.zh: 太古之上，椎輪五禮，何以異茲。

translations.literal: In highest antiquity, the five rites of the cart-wheel hub — how did they differ from this?
translations.idiomatic: In remotest antiquity, when the five rites were but the hub of a cart wheel, how were they any different from this?

sentences.zh: 太宗克晉，稍用漢禮。

translations.literal: When Taizong conquered Jin, he slightly employed Han rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong conquered the Jin territories, he gradually adopted Chinese ritual forms.

sentences.zh: 今國史院有金陳大任《遼禮儀志》，皆其國俗之故，又有《遼朝雜禮》，漢儀為多。

translations.literal: Now the National History Institute has Jin Chen Daren's "Liao Ritual Treatise," all recording their national customs of old; there is also "Miscellaneous Liao Rites," mostly Han ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The National History Institute now holds Chen Daren's Jin-dynasty "Liao Ritual Treatise," which records their native customs, and also a "Miscellaneous Liao Rites," largely in the Chinese style.

sentences.zh: 別得宣文閣所藏耶律儼《志》，視大任為加詳。

translations.literal: Separately obtained was Yelü Yan's "Treatise" held in the Xuanwen Pavilion, more detailed than Daren's.
translations.idiomatic: We also obtained Yelü Yan's treatise from the Xuanwen Pavilion collection, which is fuller than Daren's.

sentences.zh: 存其略，著於篇。

translations.literal: Preserving the outline, it is set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: We preserve the essentials here in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 祭山儀：設天神、地祇位於木葉山，東向；

translations.literal: Mountain Sacrifice Rite: The seats of the Heavenly Spirit and Earthly Spirits were set at Mount Muye, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: Mountain Sacrifice Rite: Seats for the Heavenly Spirit and Earthly Spirits were placed on Mount Muye, facing east;

sentences.zh: 中立君樹，前植群樹，以像朝班；

translations.literal: in the center stood the lord-tree; before it were planted many trees to represent the court ranks;
translations.idiomatic: a lord-tree stood at the center, with rows of trees planted before it to represent the court assembly;

sentences.zh: 又偶植二樹，以為神門。

translations.literal: and a pair of trees was planted to serve as the spirit gate.
translations.idiomatic: and two trees were paired to form the spirit gate.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后至，夷離畢具禮儀。

translations.literal: When the emperor and empress arrived, the Yelübi prepared all ritual arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and empress arrived, the Yelübi had all ritual arrangements in readiness.

sentences.zh: 牲用赭白馬、玄牛、赤白羊，皆牡。

translations.literal: Victims used were russet-white horses, black cattle, and red-white sheep — all male.
translations.idiomatic: The offerings were russet-white horses, black cattle, and red-and-white sheep, all male animals.

sentences.zh: 仆臣曰旗鼓拽剌，殺牲，體割，懸之君樹。

translations.literal: Servants called qigu zhuala slaughtered the victims, cut the carcasses, and hung them on the lord-tree.
translations.idiomatic: Servants known as qigu zhuala slaughtered the victims, butchered the carcasses, and hung the portions on the lord-tree.

sentences.zh: 太巫以酒酹牲。

translations.literal: The chief shaman libated wine over the victims.
translations.idiomatic: The chief shaman poured libations of wine over the victims.

sentences.zh: 禮官曰敵烈麻都，奏「儀辦」。

translations.literal: The ritual officer called Dirimadu reported, "The rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officer Dirimadu announced, "The rites are ready."

sentences.zh: 皇帝服金文金冠，白綾袍，絳帶，懸魚，三山絳垂，飾犀玉刀錯，絡縫烏靴。

translations.literal: The emperor wore a gold-inscribed golden crown, white gauze robe, crimson belt, suspended fish pendant, three-peaked crimson pendants, ornaments of rhinoceros horn and jade on the sword hilt, and black boots with stitched netting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore a gold-inlaid golden crown, a white gauze robe, a crimson belt with fish pendant and triple crimson pendants, a sword hilt adorned with rhinoceros horn and jade, and black boots with stitched trim.

sentences.zh: 皇后禦絳末，絡縫紅袍，懸玉佩，雙結帕，絡縫烏靴。

translations.literal: The empress wore crimson finery, a red robe with stitched netting, suspended jade pendants, a double-knotted kerchief, and black boots with stitched netting.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wore crimson regalia, a red robe with stitched trim, jade pendants at her belt, a double-knotted kerchief, and matching black boots.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后禦鞍馬。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress mounted saddled horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress then mounted their horses.

sentences.zh: 群臣在南，命婦在北，服從各部旗幟之色以從。

translations.literal: Ministers were in the south, titled ladies in the north, their dress following the colors of each department's banners.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers stood to the south and the titled ladies to the north, each arrayed in the colors of their departmental banners.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后至君樹前下馬，升南壇禦榻坐。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress dismounted before the lord-tree, ascended the southern altar, and sat on the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: At the lord-tree the emperor and empress dismounted, ascended the southern altar, and took their seats on the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 群臣命婦分班，以次入就位；

translations.literal: Ministers and titled ladies formed ranks and entered their places in order;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and titled ladies entered in ranks and took their places in order;

sentences.zh: 合班，拜訖，復位。

translations.literal: ranks united, bowed, and returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: then the assembly bowed together and returned to their stations.

sentences.zh: 皇帝皇后詣天神、地祇位，致奠；

translations.literal: The emperor and empress went to the seats of the Heavenly Spirit and Earthly Spirits and presented offerings;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress proceeded to the Heavenly and Earthly Spirit seats and presented offerings;

sentences.zh: 閣門使讀祝訖，復位坐。

translations.literal: the Gate Attendant read the prayer text; when finished, they returned to their seats.
translations.idiomatic: the Gate Attendant read the prayer, after which they returned to their seats.

sentences.zh: 北府宰相及惕隱以次致奠於君樹，遍及群樹。

translations.literal: The Northern Chancellor and the Tigu in turn presented offerings at the lord-tree, extending to all the trees.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Chancellor and the Tigu then presented offerings at the lord-tree and at each of the attendant trees in turn.

sentences.zh: 樂作。

translations.literal: Music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Music began.

sentences.zh: 群臣、命婦退。

translations.literal: Ministers and titled ladies withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers and titled ladies withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皇帝率孟父、仲父、季父之族，三匝神門樹；

translations.literal: The emperor led the clans of eldest, middle, and youngest paternal uncles three circuits around the spirit-gate trees;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led the clans of eldest, middle, and youngest uncles three times around the spirit-gate trees;

sentences.zh: 餘族七匝。

translations.literal: the remaining clans made seven circuits.
translations.idiomatic: while the other clans made seven circuits.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后再拜，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress bowed twice; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress bowed twice, and all present bowed twice with them.

sentences.zh: 上香，再拜如初。

translations.literal: Incense was offered; they bowed twice as before.
translations.idiomatic: They offered incense and bowed twice again as before.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后升壇，禦龍文方茵坐。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress ascended the altar and sat on the dragon-pattern square mat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress ascended the altar and sat on the square mat bearing the dragon pattern.

sentences.zh: 再聲警，詣祭東所，群臣、命婦從，班列如初。

translations.literal: At the second sounding of the guard, they went to the eastern sacrifice site; ministers and titled ladies followed, ranks as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the second call of the guard they proceeded to the eastern sacrifice hall, followed by ministers and titled ladies in their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 巫衣白衣，惕隱以素巾拜而冠之，巫三致辭。

translations.literal: The shaman wore white robes; the Tigu bowed and placed a plain kerchief on the shaman's head; the shaman delivered three invocations.
translations.idiomatic: The shaman dressed in white; the Tigu bowed and crowned the shaman with a plain kerchief; the shaman uttered three invocations.

sentences.zh: 每致辭，皇帝、皇后一拜，在位者皆一拜。

translations.literal: At each invocation the emperor and empress bowed once; all in attendance bowed once.
translations.idiomatic: At each invocation the emperor and empress bowed once, and all present bowed once with them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后各舉酒二爵，肉二器，再奠。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress each raised two cups of wine and two vessels of meat, and presented offerings again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress each raised two cups of wine and two vessels of meat and presented offerings again.

sentences.zh: 大臣、命婦右持酒，左持肉各一器，少後立，一奠。

translations.literal: Ministers and titled ladies held wine in the right hand and meat in the left, one vessel each, stood slightly behind, and presented one offering.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and titled ladies held wine in the right hand and meat in the left, one vessel each, stood slightly behind, and presented a single offering.

sentences.zh: 命惕隱東向擲之。

translations.literal: The Tigu was ordered to cast them eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The Tigu was commanded to cast the offerings toward the east.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后六拜，在位者皆六拜。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress bowed six times; all in attendance bowed six times.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress bowed six times, and all present bowed six times with them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后復位，坐。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress returned to position and sat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress returned to their seats.

sentences.zh: 命中丞奉茶果、餅餌各二器奠於天神、地祇位。

translations.literal: The Central Attendant was ordered to present tea, fruit, and cakes, two vessels each, as offerings at the Heavenly Spirit and Earthly Spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Attendant was ordered to present two vessels each of tea, fruit, and cakes as offerings at the Heavenly and Earthly Spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 執事郎君二十人持福酒、胙肉，詣皇帝、皇后前。

translations.literal: Twenty attendant gentlemen bore blessed wine and sacrificial meat and came before the emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty attendant gentlemen brought blessed wine and sacrificial meat before the emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 太巫奠酹訖，皇帝、皇后再拜，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: When the chief shaman had finished the libation, the emperor and empress bowed twice; all in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: After the chief shaman completed the libation, the emperor and empress bowed twice, and all present bowed twice with them.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后一拜，飲福，受胙，復位，坐。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress bowed once, drank the blessing, received the sacrificial meat, returned to position, and sat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress bowed once, drank the blessed wine, received the sacrificial meat, returned to their seats, and sat down.

sentences.zh: 在位者以次飲。

translations.literal: Those in attendance drank in order.
translations.idiomatic: Those present drank in turn.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后率群臣復班位，再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress led the ministers back to their ranks and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress led the ministers back into ranks and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 聲蹕，一拜。

translations.literal: The guard was sounded; they bowed once.
translations.idiomatic: At the sounding of the guard they bowed once.

sentences.zh: 退。

translations.literal: They withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rite concluded with their withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸幽州大悲閣，遷白衣觀音像，建廟木葉山，尊為家神。

translations.literal: Taizong visited the Dabei Pavilion in Youzhou, moved the white-robed Guanyin image, built a temple on Mount Muye, and honored it as the household spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong visited the Great Compassion Pavilion in Youzhou, moved a white-robed image of Guanyin, built a temple on Mount Muye, and honored it as the dynastic household deity.

sentences.zh: 於拜山儀過樹之後，增詣菩薩堂儀一節，然後拜神，非胡剌可汗之故也。

translations.literal: After the tree-passing in the Mountain Sacrifice Rite, a section was added for visiting the Bodhisattva Hall, and only then were the spirits worshipped — this was not Khala Khan's original practice.
translations.idiomatic: After the tree-passing in the Mountain Sacrifice Rite, a visit to the Bodhisattva Hall was added before worship of the spirits — a change not dating to Khala Khan's time.

sentences.zh: 興宗先有事於菩薩堂及木葉山遼河神，然後行拜山儀，冠服、節文多所變更，後因以為常。

translations.literal: Xingzong first performed rites at the Bodhisattva Hall and to the Liao River spirit on Mount Muye, then conducted the Mountain Sacrifice Rite; caps, robes, and ritual stages were much altered, and this later became the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong first performed rites at the Bodhisattva Hall and to the Liao River spirit on Mount Muye before conducting the Mountain Sacrifice Rite; he altered regalia and ritual stages extensively, and these changes later became standard.

sentences.zh: 神主樹木，懸牲告辦，班位奠祝，致嘏飲福，往往暗合於禮。

translations.literal: Spirit-lords in trees, hanging victims to announce readiness, ranked positions for offerings and prayers, bestowing blessings and drinking blessed wine — these often tacitly accorded with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit-lords represented by trees, hanging victims to signal readiness, ranked stations for offerings and prayers, and the bestowal and drinking of blessed portions often tacitly accorded with orthodox ritual.

sentences.zh: 天理人情，放諸四海而準，信矣夫。

translations.literal: Heavenly principle and human feeling, set forth across the four seas as the standard — truly so!
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly principle and human feeling, when set forth as a standard for all under heaven, prove themselves true indeed.

sentences.zh: 興宗更制，不能正以經術，無以大過於昔，故不載。

translations.literal: Xingzong's revised system could not be rectified by canonical learning and did not greatly surpass the past, so it is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong's revised rites could not be grounded in canonical learning and did not greatly surpass the earlier forms, and so are not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 瑟瑟儀：若旱，擇吉日行瑟瑟儀以祈雨。

translations.literal: Sese Rite: If there was drought, an auspicious day was chosen to perform the Sese Rite to pray for rain.
translations.idiomatic: Sese Rite: In time of drought, an auspicious day was chosen to perform the Sese Rite to pray for rain.

sentences.zh: 前期，置百柱天棚。

translations.literal: In advance a hundred-pillared celestial canopy was set up.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand a hundred-pillared canopy was erected.

sentences.zh: 及期，皇帝致奠於先帝御容，乃射柳。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, the emperor presented offerings before the portrait of the late emperor, then shot at the willow.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the emperor presented offerings before the late emperor's portrait, then shot at the willow target.

sentences.zh: 皇帝再射，親王、宰執以次各一射。

translations.literal: The emperor shot twice; imperial princes and chief ministers each shot once in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shot twice; imperial princes and chief ministers each shot once in succession.

sentences.zh: 中柳者質誌柳者冠服，不中者以冠服質之。

translations.literal: Whoever hit the willow pledged goods against the marker of the willow's crown and robes; whoever missed pledged crown and robes as stake.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever hit the willow won goods staked by the willow's marker; whoever missed staked his own crown and robes.

sentences.zh: 不勝者進飲於勝者，然後各歸其冠服。

translations.literal: The loser advanced to drink before the winner; then each recovered his crown and robes.
translations.idiomatic: The loser then offered a cup to the winner before each recovered his crown and robes.

sentences.zh: 又翼日，植柳天棚之東南，巫以酒醴、黍稗薦植柳，祝之。

translations.literal: On the following day a willow was planted southeast of the celestial canopy; the shaman offered wine, millet, and broomcorn millet to plant the willow and prayed.
translations.idiomatic: On the next day a willow was planted southeast of the canopy; the shaman offered wine, millet, and broomcorn millet at the planting and uttered prayers.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后祭東方畢，子弟射柳。

translations.literal: When the emperor and empress had finished sacrificing to the east, the imperial sons shot at the willow.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor and empress had completed the eastern sacrifice, the imperial sons shot at the willow.

sentences.zh: 皇族、國舅、群臣與禮者，賜物有差。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen, maternal uncles by marriage, ministers, and those participating in the rite received gifts in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen, maternal uncles of the empress, ministers, and all who took part in the rite received gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 既三日雨，則賜敵烈麻都馬四匹、衣四襲；

translations.literal: If within three days rain fell, Dirimadu was granted four horses and four suits of clothing;
translations.idiomatic: If rain fell within three days, Dirimadu was rewarded with four horses and four suits of clothing;

sentences.zh: 否則以水沃之。

translations.literal: otherwise he was doused with water.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise he was drenched with water.

sentences.zh: 道宗清寧元年，皇帝射柳訖，詣風師壇，再拜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingning under Daozong, when the emperor had finished shooting at the willow, he went to the Wind Master altar and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingning 1 (1055), after the emperor finished shooting at the willow, he went to the Wind Master altar and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 柴冊儀：擇吉日。

translations.literal: Wood-Bundle Rite: An auspicious day was chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Wood-Bundle Rite: An auspicious day was chosen.

sentences.zh: 前期，置柴冊殿及壇。

translations.literal: In advance the Wood-Bundle Hall and altar were set up.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the Wood-Bundle Hall and altar were prepared.

sentences.zh: 壇之制，厚積薪，以木為三級，壇置其上。

translations.literal: The altar's form: fuel was piled thick; a three-tiered wooden structure was made, and the altar was placed upon it.
translations.idiomatic: The altar was built by heaping fuel high, erecting a three-tiered wooden frame, and placing the altar platform on top.

sentences.zh: 席百尺氈，龍文方茵。

translations.literal: A hundred-foot felt was spread; a dragon-pattern square mat.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred-foot length of felt was spread, with a square mat bearing the dragon pattern upon it.

sentences.zh: 又置再生母後搜索之室。

translations.literal: Also set up was the Rebirth Mother's chamber for the search rite.
translations.idiomatic: A chamber was also prepared for the Rebirth Mother and the search rite.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入再生室，行再生儀畢，八部之叟前導後扈，左右扶翼皇帝冊殿之東北隅。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the rebirth chamber; when the rebirth rite was finished, elders of the Eight Tribes led before and escorted behind, supporting the emperor on left and right to the northeast corner of the Wood-Bundle Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the rebirth chamber and, when the rebirth rite was complete, elders of the Eight Tribes led before and escorted behind while attendants supported him to the northeast corner of the Wood-Bundle Hall.

sentences.zh: 拜日畢，乘馬，選外戚之老者禦。

translations.literal: When the sun-worship was finished, he mounted a horse; an elderly maternal kinsman was chosen to hold the reins.
translations.idiomatic: After the sun-worship was complete, he mounted a horse with an elderly maternal kinsman chosen to hold the reins.

sentences.zh: 皇帝疾馳，仆禦者、從者以氈覆之。

translations.literal: The emperor galloped swiftly; grooms and attendants covered him with felt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor galloped at full speed while grooms and attendants shielded him with felt coverings.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣高阜地，大臣、諸部帥列儀仗，遙望以拜。

translations.literal: The emperor went to a high mound; ministers and chieftains of the tribes arrayed ceremonial guards and bowed from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode to a high mound while ministers and tribal chieftains drew up ceremonial guards and bowed from afar.

sentences.zh: 皇帝遣使敕曰：「先帝升遐，有伯叔父兄在，當選賢者。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy with an edict saying: "The late emperor has ascended; uncles and elder brothers remain — the worthy should be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy with this edict: "The late emperor has departed; uncles and elder brothers are still among us — the worthy ought to be chosen.

sentences.zh: 沖人不德，何以為謀？

translations.literal: I, the unworthy youth — how can I be consulted in this matter?"
translations.idiomatic: I am but a youth without merit — how can I presume to counsel in this matter?"

sentences.zh: 」群臣對曰：」臣等以先帝厚恩，陛下明德，咸願盡心，敢有他圖。

translations.literal: " The ministers replied: "We, your servants, in view of the late emperor's great grace and Your Majesty's bright virtue, all wish to give our utmost devotion — who would dare harbor other designs?"
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers replied: "We, your servants, mindful of the late emperor's great grace and Your Majesty's bright virtue, are all eager to serve with full devotion and would never harbor other designs.

sentences.zh: 」皇帝令曰：「必從汝等所願，我將信明賞罰。

translations.literal: " The emperor commanded: "I must follow your wish; I will trust in clear rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor declared: "I shall heed your wish and hold to clear rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 爾有功，陟而任之；

translations.literal: If you have merit, I will promote and employ you;
translations.idiomatic: If you have merit, I will promote and employ you;

sentences.zh: 爾有罪，黜而棄之。

translations.literal: if you have guilt, I will demote and cast you aside.
translations.idiomatic: if you are guilty, I will demote and cast you aside.

sentences.zh: 若聽朕命，則當謨之。

translations.literal: If you heed my command, then deliberate on it."
translations.idiomatic: If you heed my command, then deliberate and decide."

sentences.zh: 」僉曰：「唯帝命是從。

translations.literal: " All said: "We obey only the imperial command."
translations.idiomatic: " All answered: "We obey only the imperial command."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝於所識之地，封土石以誌之。

translations.literal: " At the place the emperor recognized, he sealed earth and stone to mark it.
translations.idiomatic: " At the place the emperor had recognized, he sealed earth and stone to mark the spot.

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: Then they proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: Then the procession set out.

sentences.zh: 拜先帝御容，宴饗群臣。

translations.literal: They bowed before the late emperor's portrait and feasted the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed before the late emperor's portrait and held a feast for the ministers.

sentences.zh: 翼日，皇帝出冊殿，護衛太保扶翼升壇。

translations.literal: On the following day the emperor left the Wood-Bundle Hall; the Guard Grand Mentor supported him as he ascended the altar.
translations.idiomatic: On the next day the emperor left the Wood-Bundle Hall, and the Guard Grand Mentor supported him as he ascended the altar.

sentences.zh: 奉七廟神主置龍文方茵。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets of the seven temples were presented and placed on the dragon-pattern square mat.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets of the seven ancestral temples were brought forth and set on the square mat bearing the dragon pattern.

sentences.zh: 北、南府宰相率群臣圜立，各舉氈邊，贊祝訖，樞密使奉玉寶、玉冊入。

translations.literal: The Northern and Southern Chancellors led the ministers in a circle; each raised the edge of the felt mat; when the prayer of praise was finished, the Commissioner of Military Affairs presented the jade seal and jade book.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern and Southern Chancellors led the ministers in a circle, each holding the edge of the felt mat; when the prayer of praise was complete, the Commissioner of Military Affairs entered bearing the jade seal and jade register.

sentences.zh: 有司讀冊訖，樞密使稱尊號以進，群臣三稱萬歲，皆拜。

translations.literal: When the relevant office had finished reading the book, the Commissioner of Military Affairs proclaimed the honorific title and advanced it; the ministers thrice shouted "Ten thousand years!" and all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the appropriate office had finished reading the register, the Commissioner of Military Affairs proclaimed the honorific title and presented it; the ministers thrice shouted "Long live the emperor!" and all bowed.

sentences.zh: 宰相、北南院大王、諸部帥進赭、白羊各一群。

translations.literal: The chancellor, the great kings of the Northern and Southern Offices, and the chieftains of the tribes presented russet and white sheep, one flock each.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor, the great kings of the Northern and Southern Offices, and the tribal chieftains each presented a flock of russet and white sheep.

sentences.zh: 皇帝更衣，拜諸帝御容。

translations.literal: The emperor changed robes and bowed before the portraits of the former emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed his robes and bowed before the portraits of the former emperors.

sentences.zh: 遂宴群臣，賜賚各有差。

translations.literal: Then he feasted the ministers and bestowed gifts in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: He then feasted the ministers and distributed gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 拜日儀：皇帝升露臺，設褥，向日再拜，上香。

translations.literal: Sun-Worship Rite: The emperor ascended the open terrace, spread a mat, bowed twice toward the sun, and offered incense.
translations.idiomatic: Sun-Worship Rite: The emperor ascended the open terrace, spread a mat, bowed twice toward the sun, and offered incense.

sentences.zh: 門使通，閣使或副，應拜臣僚殿左右階陪位，再拜。

translations.literal: The Gate Attendant announced; the Pavilion Attendant or his deputy — ministers who were to bow took their places on the left and right steps of the hall and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Attendant announced; the Pavilion Attendant or his deputy called forth the ministers who were to bow, who took their places on the left and right steps of the hall and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升坐。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended and took his seat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the throne and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 奏榜訖，北班起居畢，時相已下通名再拜，不出班，奏「聖躬萬福」，又再拜，各祗候。

translations.literal: When the memorial list had been presented and the northern ranks had finished their salutation, the chief minister and those below announced their names and bowed twice without leaving rank, reported "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings," bowed twice again, and each stood at attention.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial list had been presented and the northern ranks had finished their salutation, the chief minister and those below announced their names and bowed twice without leaving rank, reported "May Your Sacred Person enjoy boundless blessings," bowed twice again, and each stood at attention.

sentences.zh: 宣徽已下橫班同。

translations.literal: The Xuanhui and those below in the cross ranks did the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanhui Commissioner and those below in the cross ranks followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 諸司、閣門、北面先奏事；

translations.literal: The various offices, the Gate Office, and the Northern Face presented business first;
translations.idiomatic: The various offices, the Gate Office, and the Northern Face presented their business first;

sentences.zh: 餘同。

translations.literal: the rest was the same.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder followed the same order.

sentences.zh: 教坊與臣僚同。

translations.literal: The Music Office followed the same procedure as the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Office followed the same procedure as the ministers.

sentences.zh: 告廟儀：至日，臣僚昧爽朝服，詣太祖廟。

translations.literal: Temple Announcement Rite: On the appointed day, at dawn ministers put on court dress and went to the Taizu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Temple Announcement Rite: On the appointed day, at dawn the ministers donned court dress and proceeded to the Taizu Temple.

sentences.zh: 次引臣僚，合班，先見御容，再拜畢，引班首左上，至褥位，再拜。

translations.literal: Next the ministers were led in; ranks united; they first viewed the imperial portrait and bowed twice; the rank leader was led up to the left, to the mat position, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were then led in, ranks united; they first viewed the imperial portrait and bowed twice; the rank leader was led up to the left to the mat position and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 贊上香，揖欄內上香畢，復褥位，再拜。

translations.literal: Incense was praised; they bowed within the railing and offered incense; when finished they returned to the mat position and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Incense was announced; they bowed within the railing and offered incense; when finished they returned to the mat position and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 各祗候立定。

translations.literal: Each stood at attention in place.
translations.idiomatic: Each stood at attention in place.

sentences.zh: 左右舉告廟祝版，於御容前跪捧。

translations.literal: Attendants on left and right raised the temple-announcement prayer board and knelt holding it before the imperial portrait.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants on the left and right raised the temple-announcement prayer board and knelt holding it before the imperial portrait.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人俯跪，讀訖，俯興，退。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Drafter knelt prostrate, read it through, rose prostrate, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Drafter knelt prostrate, read the text through, rose, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 引班首左下，復位，又再拜。

translations.literal: The rank leader was led down to the left, returned to position, and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: The rank leader was led down to the left, returned to position, and bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 分引上殿，次第進酒三。

translations.literal: They were led separately up the hall and presented wine three times in order.
translations.idiomatic: They were led separately into the hall and presented wine three times in succession.

sentences.zh: 分班引出。

translations.literal: In separate ranks they were led out.
translations.idiomatic: They were led out in separate ranks.

sentences.zh: 謁廟儀：至日昧爽，南北臣僚各具朝服，赴廟。

translations.literal: Temple Audience Rite: On the appointed day at dawn, northern and southern ministers each put on court dress and went to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Temple Audience Rite: On the appointed day at dawn, northern and southern ministers each donned court dress and proceeded to the temple.

sentences.zh: 車駕至，臣僚於門外依位序立，望駕鞠躬。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived, ministers stood outside the gate in order of rank and bowed toward the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage arrived, the ministers stood outside the gate in order of rank and bowed toward the carriage.

sentences.zh: 班首不出班，奏「聖躬萬福」。

translations.literal: The rank leader did not leave rank and reported, "May Your Sacred Person enjoy ten thousand blessings."
translations.idiomatic: The rank leader, without leaving rank, reported, "May Your Sacred Person enjoy boundless blessings."

sentences.zh: 舍人贊各祗候畢，皇帝降車，分引南北臣僚左右入，至丹墀褥位。

translations.literal: The Chamberlain praised that all were at attention; the emperor descended from the carriage; northern and southern ministers were led separately in left and right to the crimson steps mat position.
translations.idiomatic: The Chamberlain announced that all were at attention; the emperor descended from the carriage; northern and southern ministers were led separately in from left and right to the mat position on the crimson steps.

sentences.zh: 合班定，皇帝升露臺褥位。

translations.literal: Ranks united and were fixed; the emperor ascended the open terrace mat position.
translations.idiomatic: The ranks united and took their places; the emperor ascended to the mat position on the open terrace.

sentences.zh: 宣徽贊皇帝再拜，殿上下臣僚陪位皆再拜。

translations.literal: The Xuanhui praised; the emperor bowed twice; ministers above and below the hall in attendance all bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanhui Commissioner announced; the emperor bowed twice, and all ministers in attendance above and below the hall bowed twice with him.

sentences.zh: 上香畢，退，復位，再拜。

translations.literal: When incense was finished, they withdrew, returned to position, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: When the incense offering was complete, they withdrew, returned to their stations, and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 分引臣僚左右上殿位立，進御容酒依常禮。

translations.literal: Ministers were led separately left and right to their hall positions; wine was presented before the imperial portrait according to usual rite.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers were led separately to their positions left and right in the hall and presented wine before the imperial portrait according to the usual rite.

sentences.zh: 若即退，再拜。

translations.literal: If they withdrew immediately, they bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: If they withdrew at once, they bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 舍人贊「好去」，引退。

translations.literal: The Chamberlain praised "Go in peace" and led them out.
translations.idiomatic: The Chamberlain announced "Go in peace" and led them out.

sentences.zh: 禮畢。

translations.literal: The rite was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The rite was complete.

sentences.zh: 告廟、謁廟，皆曰拜容。

translations.literal: Temple announcement and temple audience were both called "bowing before the portrait."
translations.idiomatic: Temple announcement and temple audience were both called "bowing before the portrait."

sentences.zh: 以先帝、先後生辰及忌辰行禮，自太宗始也。

translations.literal: Performing rites on the birthdays and death anniversaries of the late emperor and late empress began with Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Performing rites on the birthdays and death anniversaries of the late emperor and late empress began with Taizong.

sentences.zh: 其後正旦、皇帝生辰、諸節辰皆行之。

translations.literal: Afterward New Year's Day, the emperor's birthday, and the various festival days were all observed in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter New Year's Day, the emperor's birthday, and the various festival days were all observed in the same manner.

sentences.zh: 若忌辰及車駕行幸，亦嘗遣使行禮。

translations.literal: On death anniversaries and when the imperial carriage traveled, envoys were also sometimes sent to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: On death anniversaries and when the emperor traveled, envoys were sometimes dispatched to perform the rites in his stead.

sentences.zh: 凡瑟瑟、柴冊、再生、納後則親行之。

translations.literal: For the Sese, Wood-Bundle, Rebirth, and empress-installation rites, the emperor personally performed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Sese, Wood-Bundle, Rebirth, and empress-installation rites were always performed by the emperor in person.

sentences.zh: 凡柴冊、親征則告；

translations.literal: For the Wood-Bundle rite and personal campaigns there was announcement;
translations.idiomatic: The Wood-Bundle rite and personal campaigns required temple announcement;

sentences.zh: 幸諸京則謁。

translations.literal: visits to the various capitals required audience.
translations.idiomatic: visits to the various capitals required temple audience.

sentences.zh: 四時有薦新。

translations.literal: In the four seasons there were offerings of new produce.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal offerings of new produce were made throughout the year.

sentences.zh: 孟冬朔拜陵儀：有司設酒饌於山陵。

translations.literal: First-of-Winter Tomb-Worship Rite: The relevant offices set out wine and food at the mountain tombs.
translations.idiomatic: First-of-Winter Tomb-Worship Rite: The relevant offices prepared wine and food offerings at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后駕至，敵烈麻都奏「儀辦」。

translations.literal: When the emperor and empress arrived, Dirimadu reported, "The rites are ready."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and empress arrived, Dirimadu announced, "The rites are ready."

sentences.zh: 閣門使贊皇帝、皇后詣位四拜訖，巫贊祝燔胙及時服，酹酒薦牲。

translations.literal: The Gate Attendant praised; the emperor and empress went to their positions and bowed four times; the shaman praised the prayer, burned sacrificial meat and seasonal garments, libated wine, and presented victims.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Attendant announced; the emperor and empress went to their positions and bowed four times; the shaman intoned the prayer, burned sacrificial meat and seasonal garments, poured libations, and presented victims.

sentences.zh: 大臣、命婦以次燔胙，四拜。

translations.literal: Ministers and titled ladies in turn burned sacrificial meat and bowed four times.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and titled ladies in turn burned sacrificial portions and bowed four times.

sentences.zh: 皇帝、皇后率群臣、命婦，循諸陵各三匝。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress led ministers and titled ladies three circuits around each tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress led the ministers and titled ladies three times around each tomb.

sentences.zh: 還宮。

translations.literal: They returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: They then returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 翼日，群臣入謝。

translations.literal: On the following day the ministers entered to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On the next day the ministers entered court to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 爇節儀：皇帝即位，凡征伐叛國俘掠人民，或臣下進獻人口，或犯罪沒官戶，皇帝親覽閑田，建州縣以居之，設官治其事。

translations.literal: Burning Festival Rite: When the emperor took the throne, all persons captured in campaigns against rebel states, populations presented by ministers, or households confiscated for crimes — the emperor personally surveyed idle land, established prefectures and counties to settle them, and appointed officials to govern the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Burning Festival Rite: When an emperor took the throne, all persons taken in campaigns against rebel states, populations presented by ministers, or households confiscated for crimes were settled by the emperor's personal survey of idle land; he established prefectures and counties for them and appointed officials to govern their affairs.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，所置人戶、府庫、錢粟，穹廬中置小氈殿，帝及后妃皆鑄金像納焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the households, treasuries, and grain stores he had established — within the yurt a small felt hall was set up, and golden images of the emperor and consorts were cast and placed therein.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the households, treasuries, and grain stores he had established were preserved; within the yurt a small felt hall was erected, and golden images of the emperor and his consorts were cast and placed inside.

sentences.zh: 節辰、忌日、朔望，皆致祭於穹廬之前。

translations.literal: On festival days, death anniversaries, and the first and fifteenth of the month, offerings were all presented before the yurt.
translations.idiomatic: On festival days, death anniversaries, and the first and fifteenth of each month, offerings were presented before the yurt.

sentences.zh: 又築土為臺，高丈餘，置大盤於上，祭酒食撒於其中，焚之，國俗謂之爇節。

translations.literal: Also an earthen platform more than ten feet high was built; a great basin was placed on top; sacrificial wine and food were scattered within and burned — the national custom called this the Burning Festival.
translations.idiomatic: An earthen platform more than ten feet high was also built, with a great basin placed on top; sacrificial wine and food were scattered into it and burned — a national custom known as the Burning Festival.

sentences.zh: 歲除儀：初夕，敕使及夷離畢率執事郎君至殿前，以鹽及羊膏置爐中燎之。

translations.literal: New Year's Eve Rite: On the first evening, the imperial envoy and the Yelübi led attendant gentlemen to the front of the hall; salt and sheep fat were placed in the brazier and burned.
translations.idiomatic: New Year's Eve Rite: On the first evening, the imperial envoy and the Yelübi led attendant gentlemen before the hall; salt and sheep fat were placed in the brazier and burned.

sentences.zh: 巫及大巫以次贊祝火神訖，閣門使贊皇帝面火再拜。

translations.literal: The shaman and chief shaman in turn praised the prayer to the Fire Spirit; when finished, the Gate Attendant praised; the emperor faced the fire and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The shaman and chief shaman in turn intoned the prayer to the Fire Spirit; when finished, the Gate Attendant announced, and the emperor faced the fire and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 初，皇帝皆親拜，至道宗始命夷離畢拜之。

translations.literal: At first the emperor always bowed in person; only from Daozong onward was the Yelübi ordered to bow in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor always bowed in person; only under Daozong was the Yelübi ordered to perform the bowing on his behalf.
